on_record.summary: Listed as a donor at one of the smaller giving levels.

record_funding: An autonomous institution, by its own account un-aided by government. Donors of Rs 10 crore and above: Ministry of Culture, Citibank, Bank of America, TCS Foundation, J. Paul Getty Trust.

on_record.summary: Wikipedia lists it as one of the museum’s main sponsors.

record_funding: CHF 30M budget. Basel-Stadt and Riehen give about 9%; the Beyeler Foundation covers a 27% deficit. Sponsors include UBS (Artist Talks) and Globus.

on_record.summary: Novartis calls the Kunsthaus a long-standing partner on its sponsorship page.

record_funding: Logo strip on its 2026 site: a canton BL logo, Münchenstein, Muttenz, Novartis, Basellandschaftliche Kantonalbank, Habasit, Jenzer Fleisch + Feinkost and a hotel. Novartis lists it as a long-time partner.

on_record.summary: Novartis International AG is named as a sponsor.

record_funding: Canton Basel-Stadt and the Emanuel Hoffmann, Christoph Merian and Laurenz foundations. UBS is partner; Novartis, KPMG, Trafina and the Federal Office of Culture are sponsors.

on_record.summary: Listed among partners and sponsors in the 2024-25 annual report.

record_funding: Principally funded by the NSW Government: of total revenue of $81.4 million in 2024-25, recurrent grants from the NSW Government were $46.9 million and capital grants $15.3 million. Self-generated revenue was $15.6 million, with $1.455 million in sponsorships, and the Australian Museum Foundation gave $1,116,404 (annual report 2024-25).
Run by IDG with the City of Rio and Fundação Roberto Marinho. Itaú is strategic sponsor. Shell, Instituto Cultural Vale and Motiva are maintainers. IBM, TAG and Bloomberg also give.

on_record.summary: Tequila 1800 is a 2026 sponsor (donations page, logo).

record_funding: Artist-founded non-profit (Bosco Sodi, 2014); 2026 sponsors: Harp Helú, Home Depot, Teka, Grupo Habita, Tequila 1800, Punta Pájaros, Nirox Foundation.

on_record.summary: The Fundación José Cuervo logo is on the page of the museum’s Patronato, with no amount.

record_funding: A museum of the Instituto Nacional de Bellas Artes y Literatura (INBAL), with a Patronato created in 1988 to help protect, conserve and enlarge the collection; the Patronato page shows Interceramic and Fundación José Cuervo. General admission is $95.00; the pages read did not state amounts.

First partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.

on_record.summary: Is named as a lead sponsor on the museum's support page.

record_funding: Private museum in the Rockbund development on the Bund. No funder list or budget is published.

on_record.summary: Sangeeta Jindal of the JSW Foundation is Khoj's Benefactor.

record_funding: Artist-run since 1997. Top supporters: Prince Claus Fund, Goethe-Institut New Delhi and Ford Foundation. Capital circle includes Apeejay Trust, Inlaks India Foundation, Weikfield. Benefactor Sangeeta Jindal.

on_record.summary: Pfizer Deutschland is a Corporate Friend at €5,000 a year.

record_funding: State of Berlin funds the foundation, beside admissions, book sales, sponsorship and donations. GASAG AG, DKB AG and Pfizer Deutschland GmbH are its corporate members.

on_record.summary: Gave NZ$70,000 in each of FY2019 and FY2020, NZ$50,000 in FY2021, NZ$26,000 in FY2025 and NZ$25,000 in FY2026. The gallery lists it as a strategic partner.

record_funding: Creative New Zealand (NZ$637k a year, 2027 to 2029) and Auckland Council lead. Chartwell Trust, Foundation North, Goethe-Institut and Wesfarmers partner. Pub Charity gave NZ$4,000, undated.

on_record.summary: Helps fund the festival, with Northwestel and Indigenous bodies.

record_funding: Canadian Heritage granted CAD 160,000 for 2025 to 2027; the Town of Inuvik gives the venue and over CAD 30,000 in kind. Indigenous bodies, Air North and Northwestel help; Canada Council refused about CAD 90,000 in 2026.

on_record.summary: The Digicel Foundation gave $3 million in July 2024 toward upgrading the Art District.

record_funding: Inter-American Development Bank (US$1.3M over three years), Bank of Jamaica, Digicel Foundation, Barita, Gore, National Bakery, PwC, the Clara Lionel Foundation and the Miami Foundation.
